issues.t: Rust in the windshield frame, door bottoms and rear body
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust spots around the windshield, sunroof, tail lights, door edges, rear shock towers and spring perches. Badly affected trucks show rust on crossmembers and the frame.
issues.why: Early trucks of this generation were not well protected from the factory, and the boxy steel body traps water in seams and corners. Owners report it is much more common before about 2005.
issues.next: Inspect the body and underside closely, including under trim and in the wheel wells. Small spots can be slowed with rust-proofing; deep rust in the windshield frame or frame rails is a major repair, so have a body shop inspect it before buying.

issues.t: Power window regulators fail
issues.sym: A window moves slowly, makes a grinding or clicking noise, drops into the door or stops moving altogether.
issues.why: The window regulators inside the doors wear out over time on this body style, and owners report they eventually fail regardless of mileage.
issues.next: Keep the window closed if it will not go up, and have the regulator and motor checked. Replacing one door is a common repair on these trucks.

issues.t: Door locks and door handles stop working
issues.sym: A door will not lock or unlock with the remote, a lock button acts on its own, or a handle feels loose and will not open the door.
issues.why: The door lock actuators and the handle mechanisms wear out or break. Water getting into the doors can make it worse.
issues.next: Test every door with the key, remote and interior button. A shop can replace the actuator or handle parts in the affected door.

issues.t: Recurring electrical faults on early G500s
issues.sym: Random warning lights, gauges or accessories acting up, and repeated failures of parts like the alternator, throttle sensor and transmission control unit.
issues.why: Owners of 2002 trucks report a long run of electrical glitches. Some say swapping in the engine computer and instrument cluster from a late 2003 or 2004 truck ended many of them.
issues.next: Have codes read from all modules, not just the engine. Look for an independent Mercedes specialist who knows the G-Class, since guessing at parts wastes time.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the valve covers and oil pan
issues.sym: Oil spots under the truck, a burning oil smell after driving, or oily grime on the engine and transmission.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets on the 5.0L V8 harden with age and seep oil. Owners also report leaks at the oil pan, dipstick tube and transmission pan.
issues.next: Watch the oil level. Have the leak source confirmed; valve cover gaskets are often done along with the spark plugs and plug wires.

issues.t: Front axle swivel seals leak and wheel bearings wear
issues.sym: Greasy buildup or fluid around the front hubs and axle knuckles, a leaking front differential, or play in a front wheel.
issues.why: The seals at the swivel ends of the solid front axle wear out, and the kingpin and wheel bearings develop play with age and off-road use.
issues.next: Have the front axle inspected for leaks and play. A full front axle service with new bearings and seals is a big job, so get a quote before buying.

issues.t: Worn suspension bushings, ball joints and shocks
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a loose or wandering feel, a bouncy ride, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Rubber bushings, ball joints, coil spring mounts and shocks wear out with age, even on trucks that have mostly sat.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected. Aftermarket shocks are an option and many owners use them.

issues.t: Water leaks from the sunroof and door seals
issues.sym: Wet carpet or headliner stains, a musty smell, or electronics that act strangely after rain.
issues.why: The sunroof drains clog and the sunroof and door seals age and stop sealing. Water inside the cabin can upset the electronics.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains and check the seals. Dry the carpet fully and have any affected wiring or modules checked.

issues.t: Front turn signals hard to see behind the grille guard (recall)
issues.sym: The front turn signals look dim from some angles.
issues.why: A protective grille over the front turn signals could reduce how visible the signal is, so the trucks did not meet the federal lighting standard.
issues.next: Ask a Mercedes dealer to check your VIN. The fix was free improved turn signal units.

issues.t: Fuel line connectors may not be fully seated (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A fuel smell would be a sign of a problem.
issues.why: Quick connectors on the fuel lines may not have been fully clicked together at the factory and could pull apart in a frontal crash, leaking fuel.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it towed if you smell fuel. Ask a dealer whether the free clamp has been installed.

issues.t: Passenger airbag trim strip can break loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: On trucks built from September 2010 to April 2011, a trim strip near the passenger airbag could come off and hit occupants when the airbag deploys.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers reinforce the trim strip for free.

issues.t: Knocking from the suspension on rough roads
issues.sym: A knock or clunk from the front or rear when driving over broken pavement.
issues.why: The sway bar end links wear or loosen, letting the bar knock.
issues.next: Have the end links checked for play. They are a fairly simple part to replace.

issues.t: Engine misfires when accelerating
issues.sym: The engine stumbles or shakes under hard acceleration, and the check engine light may flash.
issues.why: Spark plug boots can leak and let air in, so the spark does not reach the plug properly when the engine is under load.
issues.next: Avoid hard acceleration if the light is flashing. Have the misfire codes read and the plugs, boots and coils checked.

issues.t: Steering coupling may be loose and wear (recall)
issues.sym: Play or a clunk in the steering, or steering that feels vague.
issues.why: The coupling in the steering shaft may not have been tightened enough at the factory. It can wear and, in the worst case, affect steering control.
issues.next: Get the free recall repair as soon as possible. Owners first got interim letters, so confirm the new coupling was actually fitted.

issues.t: Inside door handle cable can break (recall)
issues.sym: A door will not open from the inside when you pull the handle.
issues.why: The cable between the inner handle and the latch can snap if the door is hard to open, such as after a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the cables in all four doors for free.

issues.t: Engine may not cut power when stability control acts with Distronic on (recall)
issues.sym: With adaptive cruise control on, the truck may not slow as expected when the stability system steps in.
issues.why: A stability control (ESP) software fault could stop the engine from reducing power while Distronic Plus is engaged, making stopping distances longer.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers reprogram the ESP control unit for free.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum hose can collapse (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and you need to push much harder to stop.
issues.why: The vacuum hose that feeds the brake booster could collapse, cutting power assist to the brakes.
issues.next: A hard brake pedal means the brake assist has failed, so the car needs much more force and distance to stop. If it happens while driving, press the pedal firmly, slow down and pull off the road when it's safe. Don't keep driving it: have it towed to a dealer. The hose is replaced for free under the recall.

issues.t: Emergency call system may send the wrong location (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in daily driving.
issues.why: Software in the communication module may report the wrong location to emergency responders after a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN. The free fix is a software update done over the air or by a dealer.

issues.t: Emergency call system can stop working from a SIM software error (recall)
issues.sym: An SOS or emergency call warning may appear, or the system simply cannot connect.
issues.why: A software error on the SIM card can stop the module from connecting to the mobile network, disabling automatic crash calls.
issues.next: Check your VIN. The free fix is a software update.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky downshifts
issues.sym: A jolt or kick when the 9-speed automatic downshifts while slowing down, often in lower gears, or a delayed shift in traffic.
issues.why: Owners report this on both G550 and AMG G63 models. Dealers often call it normal; fixes tried include software updates and resetting the transmission adaptation, and in at least one case the transmission was replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Note when it happens and ask the dealer for a transmission software check and adaptation reset. If it keeps happening, ask for deeper diagnostics while the truck is under warranty.

issues.t: Rear door latches may not latch or open (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door looks closed but is not fully latched, or will not open from inside.
issues.why: Parts inside the rear door latches can keep them from catching or releasing properly, so a door could open while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recall 21V-353 and 24V-659. Trucks fixed under the first recall need the newer latch too.

issues.t: Front axle wiring can rub on the oil cooler and disable ABS (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, ESP or brake warning lights, and stability control not available.
issues.why: The wiring harness at the front axle can chafe against the oil cooler until it is damaged, cutting anti-lock brakes and stability control.
issues.next: Get the free recall done soon. Dealers inspect the harness and add a protective sleeve or replace it.

issues.t: Turbocharger oil feed line can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell or oily residue around the turbochargers.
issues.why: The oil line feeding the turbos on the AMG 4.0L V8 can leak oil onto hot exhaust parts, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell burning oil and contact a dealer. The line is replaced for free.

issues.t: Differential lock module can knock out ABS and stability control (recall)
issues.sym: ABS and ESP warning lights come on.
issues.why: A resistor inside the differential locking control module may fail and shut off anti-lock brakes and stability control.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers inspect and replace the module as needed for free.

issues.t: Fuel rail and injectors can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the engine.
issues.why: Particles trapped between the fuel rail and injectors during manufacturing can cause a fuel leak, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Dealers replace the fuel rail and injectors for free.

issues.t: Powertrain computer can reset and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may shut off while driving.
issues.why: The central powertrain controller can reset itself while the truck is moving.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers update the software for free.

issues.t: Side crash sensor connectors can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: Connectors on the side impact sensors may loosen, delaying the side airbags and seat belt tensioners in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers inspect and replace the sensors as needed for free.

issues.t: Fuel pump can shut down and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or suddenly loses power while driving, and may not restart.
issues.why: The fuel pump can stop working while driving. Mercedes recalled many 2021-2024 models for this under recalls 23V-445 and 23V-880.
issues.next: If the engine cuts out, get safely off the road. Check your VIN for both recalls; the fuel pump is replaced for free.

issues.t: A/C may have been filled with the wrong refrigerant (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom. Weak air conditioning can be a sign of a leak.
issues.why: Some trucks were filled with the wrong refrigerant, which can leak and raises the fire risk in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers replace the refrigerant for free.

issues.t: Rear differential housing can crack on 4x4 Squared models (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the rear axle, or noise and loss of drive from the rear.
issues.why: On AMG G63 4x4 Squared special editions, the rear axle differential housing can crack and leak or break, which can cause loss of control.
issues.next: Do not drive the truck until the recall is done. Mercedes offers towing and a loaner, and the repair is free.

issues.t: Front radar sensor can fail and disable safety systems (recall)
issues.sym: Warnings that automatic emergency braking, lane keeping or Distronic cruise control are not available.
issues.why: The circuit board in the front short-range radar sensor may fail, shutting off several driver assistance features.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers replace the sensor for free.

issues.t: Stability control may show the wrong warning light (recall)
issues.sym: If the stability system fails, the dashboard may not show the correct warning.
issues.why: Software in the stability control (ESP) unit may display an incorrect warning light during a fault.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers update the ESP software for free.

issues.t: Wrong wheel bolts may have been fitted (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration or a clunking from a wheel, or a wheel that feels loose.
issues.why: Incorrect wheel bolts may have been installed on some electric G580 models, so a wheel could loosen or come off.
issues.next: Stop driving if you feel vibration from a wheel. Dealers replace the wheel bolts for free.
